# TrustyNavigationTabs

`Navigation` · composition depth: `base`

A vertical rail of tabs that stands beside the region it drives — the settings-dialog sidebar, the tool toolbar. Always vertical, so arrow keys run up and down. The active tab takes a filled wash and a bar on the rail's outer edge, which is what makes it read as a place you are rather than a control you pressed. Each tab's 'value' doubles as the name of the slot holding its panel; leave the slot out and you get a rail-only strip you drive externally through v-model.

It is the same machinery as TrustyTabs — same Reka primitive, same tab semantics — dressed as a navigation rail. Reach for it when the strip is the frame around the content rather than a control inside it.

**Use it when**
- a persistent sidebar swaps a large content region beside it, like a settings dialog
- an icon rail picks the active tool or view and stays on screen while you work

**Don't use it for**
- an inline strip above the region it swaps: use TrustyTabs, which runs horizontally too
- items that are real destinations and change the URL: use plain links, so they can be middle-clicked, copied and land fresh
- a value the user sets rather than a view they switch to: use TrustyToggleGroup
- groups that may all stand open at once: use TrustyAccordion
- hierarchical content: use TrustyTree

```ts
import { TrustyNavigationTabs } from '@louislp/trusty-ui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `{ value: T; label?: string \| undefined; icon?: `${string}:${string}` \| undefined; disabled?: boolean \| undefined; }[]` | *required* | The tabs, in order. Each tab: - `value`: unique value v-model reports for the active tab; also the name of the slot that fills this tab's panel (one named slot per value; omit the slot to render no panel — rail-only, content driven externally via v-model) and the a11y name of an icon-only tab - `label`: text (omit for icon-only) - `icon`: icon name (Iconify `collection:icon`, e.g. `ph:gear`) - `disabled`: disable just this tab |
| `placement` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Which side the rail is docked to. The active bar takes the rail's outer edge, away from the panel. |
| `size` | `"md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"` |  |
| `modelValue` | `T` | — |  |

## Events

- `update:modelValue` — `[value: T \| undefined]`

## Examples in Storybook

- Default — The default rail — docked left, bar on its outer edge, panel to the right.
- KeyboardNavigation — Interaction test — clicking a tab swaps the panel, arrow keys run up and down the rail skipping the disabled tab, and only the selected trigger is in the tab order (roving tabindex). This is what the Tabs primitive buys us over a plain list of links; the test is here to catch a regression that quietly takes it away.
- Right — Docked right — mirror of the default; the bar flips to the rail's other outer edge.
- Icons — Icon beside label — the settings-sidebar shape.
- Large — `lg` scale — taller triggers, 14px labels.
- ExtraLarge — `xl` scale — tallest triggers, 18px labels, 24px icons.
- DisabledTab — A disabled tab is skipped by keyboard nav and can't be activated.
- IconRail — Icon-only rail — no labels, so each `value` is the tab's accessible name. Triggers collapse to a square.
- RailOnly — Rail only — no panel slots. Drive content living outside the component via `v-model`.
